title: Duke Nukem: Time to Kill
synopsis: n-Space’s third-person Duke Nukem for PlayStation — retained so the console’s licensed action shelf records more than a single port of the PC shooter.

catalog.mediumForm: Pressed optical disc · PlayStation retail edition

custody.physical: Complete in box: case, pressed disc, manual, and original cover insert
custody.condition: Complete in box. Light shelf wear consistent with age. Preserved as a playable reference copy.

curatorNotes:
Duke Nukem: Time to Kill is not a conversion of the PC shooter that made the character famous on this generation. It is a PlayStation-built third-person game — n-Space’s own construction under GT Interactive — and that distinction matters on a shelf that also holds Total Meltdown.

Kept alone, either title would imply that Duke’s PlayStation presence was a single idea. Together they record two different answers to the same license: one a console edition of Duke Nukem 3D, the other a new third-person campaign built for this hardware’s audience and its controllers.

The filing is custody of that second answer. It belongs here so the Original PlayStation collection can show how a major late-nineties action property was localized onto Sony’s disc format without collapsing every release into one story.
collectionNotes:
Acquired in August 2026 while establishing the first Duke Nukem pair on the Original PlayStation shelf.

The retained copy is the North American PlayStation edition published by GT Interactive (SLUS-00583). It remains complete in box with manual and cover insert, and is kept beside Duke Nukem: Total Meltdown as the reference set for this license on the platform.

Dedicated artifact views of the individual copy have not yet been filed; the gallery below is held open for that documentation.

preservation.playableOn: Sony PlayStation; compatible North American PlayStation hardware
preservation.compatibility: Pressed for North American PlayStation consoles. The retained disc remains the primary access copy.
preservation.concerns: Optical-disc aging and surface damage remain the principal risks. The disc is stored upright in its original case under stable, dry conditions; printed materials remain housed with the copy.
preservation.knownRevisions: North American PlayStation release published by GT Interactive in October 1998 (SLUS-00583), developed by n-Space. European territories received separate PlayStation localizations under GT Interactive.
preservation.availability: The original physical edition is out of print and circulates through the secondary market. No current digital edition replaces this reference copy.
